method: Logistic regression of destroyed on DINS-coded hardening features, year-built era and fire fixed effects (Newton-Raphson, numpy), fitted on every fire except the holdout. Unknown values are kept as their own level. Observed ratios are fire-stratified; each fire is scored by a model fitted without it. model_implied_ratio converts the engine's risk ratio to an odds ratio at the unfavourable group's destroyed share.
data_source: CAL FIRE Damage Inspection (DINS) database, ArcGIS FeatureServer https://services1.arcgis.com/jUJYIo9tSA7EHvfZ/ArcGIS/rest/services/POSTFIRE_MASTER_DATA_SHARE/FeatureServer/0
data_vintage: DINS layer last edited 2026-01-06; 32 fires, 2015 to 2025; seeded sample of 12,362 single residences
verdict: Class A roof, enclosed eaves and screened vents each lower the destroyed share within a fire, and the engine's 8% credit per feature understates all three. Zone 0 clearance cannot be tested in DINS. Hardening features alone discriminate weakly (mean AUC 0.55 current, 0.63 refit on complete-case homes; Palisades holdout 0.53 vs 0.57). DINS attributes are recorded after the fire, so Unknown mostly marks destroyed homes.
